newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African bond and currency markets continued to consolidate on Wednesday with bond and currency traders reporting tight trading ranges and good underlying market sentiment.

On the bond market, the yield on the benchmark R150 bond was just below the 15 percent figure at 1425 GMT at 14.975 percent from 14.93 percent late on Tuesday after holding in a tight 14.94 to 15.00 percent range on the day.
Bond traders said the yield on the key bond ticked higher at the start of trade after the yield on the U.S. T-bond rose above the key seven percent level amid renewed fears of a U.S. rate hike.
The Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, where a decision to raise interest rates is expected, will be held on September 24.

On Tuesday, an unidentified Federal Reserve official told Reuters that eight out of 12 Fed banks had asked for an increase in the discount rate. This sent the 30-year Treasury bond nearly a full point lower and its yield rose above the psychologically important 7 percent level.
"The guys held off a bit today after U.S. came off overnight but after local rates initially ticked up we saw some good buying at the 15 percent figure," a trader noted.
Underlying sentiment was relatively bullish and the market was seen continuing a period of consolidation which set in around Tuesday this week after sharp downward moves last Friday.

"In the longer-term there are more bulls than bears in the market and we're expecting more downward momentum...a surprise in the CPI figure tomorrow (Thursday) could trigger some activity and the market will also be watching U.S. rates," the trader added.
Economists polled by Reuters expect August consumer price inflation figures, due out at 0900 GMT on Thursday, to rise to 7.7 percent year-on-year from 7.1 percent in July.
The month-on-month rate of increase was seen little changed at 0.7 percent from 0.8 percent in July.

Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners turned net buyers of 384.62 million rand worth of South African bonds after a net selling position of 38.57 million rand on Tuesday and 266.98 million rand on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were 4.79 bilion rand on Tuesday from 5.11 billion rand on Monday.
It was another listless day on the local currency market as the rand clung to a tight 4.48 to 4.49 trading range after briefly following bonds weaker.
Dealers commented on the unit's inability to break 4.48 on the bottom and 4.49 at the top, noting that the current stability looked set to continue.
"It looks as if we will move in these ranges for some time. At the moment we are seeing a fair match of importer demand for dollars but also dollars coming in from offshore," a senior trader said.
There had been no sign of the Reserve Bank for a while, he said, which was only expected to show its hand if the rand moved above 4.50 on the dollar.
The market would be watching the dollar ahead of the FOMC meeting next Tuesday for fresh direction but it was unlikely that events in the U.S. would shatter the rand's stability, dealers said.

The unit ended the day at 4.4850/4900 from 4.4840/4890 late on Tuesday. Against the crosses, the currency was last trading at 6.9984/7.0093 against sterling from 6.9704/9804 late on Tuesday and at 0.3358/3364 marks from 0.3374/3379 marks previously.

On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent while 90-day BAs were also unchanged at between 15.20 to 15.40 percent. The Reserve Bank put the daily shortage at 7.315 billion rand on Tuesday from 7.931 billion rand on Monday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
